lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Portland businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Portland is a city of neighbourhoods and independent businesses, with a design-minded population that is sceptical of advertising and loyal to companies it believes in. We plan marketing that suits that audience: specific, honest and rooted in the part of town you serve.

sections.heading: A city organised by neighbourhood
paragraphs: The Willamette River splits Portland into west and east, and residents identify strongly with their own quarter. On the west side are downtown, the Pearl District with its converted warehouses, and the shops along Northwest 23rd. Across the river, commercial streets carry the life of the city: Hawthorne, Division, Alberta, Mississippi, Belmont. Sellwood and St. Johns feel like small towns of their own.

People shop, eat and book services close to home, often on foot or by bike, and they search with the neighbourhood or street name. The suburbs behave differently. Beaverton and Hillsboro to the west are home to sportswear and semiconductor employers and their well-paid staff, Lake Oswego and West Linn are affluent residential areas, and Gresham lies to the east. Vancouver, Washington, is just across the Columbia, and its residents cross into Oregon to shop without sales tax.

sections.heading: What the Portland economy is made of
paragraphs: Athletic and outdoor companies have made the region a centre for footwear and apparel design, and a large community of designers, agencies and suppliers works around them. Chip manufacturing and software give the western suburbs the nickname Silicon Forest. A large academic medical centre sits on the hill above downtown, and the port and freight yards along the rivers handle trade.

Alongside those sit the small firms Portland is known for: coffee roasters, breweries, food carts, bakeries, bike builders, bookshops, makers of leather goods, ceramics and furniture. Many began at a market stall and now sell nationally online.

sections.heading: Marketing to people who distrust marketing
paragraphs: Portlanders tend to reward businesses that are independent, transparent and consistent with their stated values, and they share opinions freely in reviews and on neighbourhood forums. Polished but empty advertising falls flat. What works is detail: who makes the product, where materials come from, what a service includes and what it costs.
bullets: Pages that explain your process and pricing approach in plain terms.
Original photography and video in place of stock images.
Local search built around neighbourhoods and streets, with an accurate Google Business Profile.
Social content that sounds like the people who run the business.
Paid campaigns tested in small steps and judged on sales, not impressions.

sections.heading: Rain, roses and the summer rush
paragraphs: The long wet season shapes daily habits. Through autumn and winter, people spend more time indoors and online, and roofers, gutter cleaners and heating firms are in demand. An occasional ice storm brings the city to a halt and sends searches for tree removal and plumbers soaring. Once the dry weather arrives, patios, street fairs, farmers markets and outdoor events fill up, the Rose Festival marks early summer, and visitors come for the food, the beer and day trips to the Gorge, the coast and Mount Hood. Restaurants, tour operators and retailers do well to have summer content and ads ready in spring.

faqs.q: How do I rank for searches in my Portland neighbourhood?
faqs.a: Keep your business profile complete, mention your neighbourhood and nearby streets naturally on your site, earn reviews from local customers and get listed by neighbourhood associations and local publications where you can.

faqs.q: Can I advertise to shoppers from Vancouver, Washington?
faqs.a: Yes. Ads and pages can target Clark County residents, and for larger purchases it is reasonable to point out that Oregon has no sales tax. Check the wording with your accountant if you are unsure.

faqs.q: What kind of social media content works in Portland?
faqs.a: Content that shows the real business: the people, the process and the neighbourhood. Behind-the-scenes video and straightforward answers to customer questions tend to do better than heavily produced promotion.

faqs.q: How much does a Portland marketing campaign cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the channels and the amount of creative work involved. We set out a quote after a free consultation about your goals.
